1,000-page metadata plan does not render.detail: tests/browser/large-mobile.spec.ts test 1 opens a real generated 1,000-page PDF through the public workspace and asserts the page list mounts at most 48 rows (WINDOW_SIZE windowing in PagePicker), that a far page (950) stays reachable via the jump input, and that select-all is honestly capped at 20 with the limit notice visible. run.json records 6/6 passed including this leg.

selected native/OCR limits visible.detail: tests/browser/large-mobile.spec.ts test 2 asserts the run-limits disclosure (data-testid=run-limits) shows the active profile and every enforced bound: file cap, document cap, native pages per run, OCR pages per run, raster pixel cap. The mobile-profile leg additionally asserts the explicit OCR consent control and the OCR-cap notices already present in OpenWorkspace.

320px and touch controls usable.detail: tests/browser/large-mobile.spec.ts test 3 runs at a real 320x568 viewport: the mobile profile engages, page toggles measure >=44px, no horizontal overflow (scrollWidth == clientWidth), the OCR consent row renders, preview is on-demand, and the run remains startable. The page-change regression test added at c132da6 verifies a stale preview raster is cleared when the preview page changes.

oversized edges rejected before allocati.detail: tests/browser/large-mobile.spec.ts test 4 offers a >20 MiB candidate (rejected on declared size before byte reads, intake surface preserved) and a 1,001-page document (rejected with the too_many_pages error). The adapter's pre-allocation raster cap is exercised by the preview path; nothing allocates before the guards pass.

cancellation leaves coherent partial res.detail: tests/browser/large-mobile.spec.ts test 5 starts a multi-page run, cancels it mid-flight, asserts the honest cancelled state, returns to selection, then opens a different PDF through the confirmed replacement path (pages-summary shows 2 pages). Generation-first cleanup prevents stale writes.
